questions.question: Placental mammals in Australia has variable forms which appears to be ‘similar’ to a corresponding marsupial. This is a case of:
questions.explanation: (B) In Australia, placental mammals evolved into various forms, each resembling a similar marsupial counterpart. This is an example of convergent evolution, where unrelated species evolve similar traits due to similar environmental pressures. Meanwhile, the diversity within each group (placental mammals and marsupials) shows adaptive radiation, where species diversify to fill different ecological niches. [New NCERT Class 12th Page no. 116, 117]

questions.explanation: (3) Placental wolf and Tasmanian wolf marsupial exhibit convergent evolution. [New NCERT Class 12th Page no. 118]

questions.question: An evolutionary pattern characterised by a rapid increase in number of kinds of closely related species is called
questions.explanation: The evolutionary pattern characterized by a rapid increase in the number of kinds of closely related species is called Adaptive radiation. Adaptive radiation refers to the process where a single ancestral species rapidly diversifies into a wide variety of forms to adapt to different environments. This leads to the formation of several new species in a relatively short period of time, each adapted to a specific ecological niche. A classic example of adaptive radiation is seen in Darwin's finches, which evolved into various species with different beak shapes suited to different food sources.
